key_insight: Platinum photoelectron spectra are shaped by a mix of intrinsic lifetime broadening, satellite losses, and strong relativistic effects, which must all be modeled together to correctly assign features.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a reliable spectral reference for platinum and Pt-based materials, improving interpretation of catalyst and electronic-material characterization by XPS/HAXPES.
method: RHEELS to map loss features and plasmon-related excitations
SXPS and HAXPES to measure shallow and deep core-level line shapes
DFT and G0W0 calculations, with spin-orbit coupling, to reproduce valence-band structure
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic comparison of multiple spectroscopies with ab initio calculations, identifying previously unresolved satellite features and confirming assignments across the Pt spectrum.
watch_item: Spectral interpretation depends on careful separation of overlapping satellites, plasmon losses, and spin-orbit splittings, so transfer to other instruments or sample conditions may require revalidation.
paper_title: Lifetime effects and satellites in the photoelectron spectrum of platinum metal
